chunks: And with this chain of narration, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
"Whoever is tested with the role of a judge, let him be equal among them in gesture, in gaze, and in seating."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.الْقَضَاءِ: Judiciary / The role of a judge

ai.seo_question: What are the physical signs of judicial impartiality in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) emphasizes that judicial impartiality extends beyond legal rulings to include subtle physical cues such as gestures, gaze, and seating arrangement. This guidance underscores the Shia scholarly understanding that visible equity prevents litigants from suspecting bias, thereby preserving the integrity and legitimacy of the judge's authority.
